I'm not a huge fan of long lists of rules, if I was I'd still be hanging out on that other place, but here's my take.

Subverses are overseen by moderators who set the topics, rules and guidelines for the subverse. The reality is that mods can set as many, or as few, rules/guidelines they want and subscribers will accept - as long as it's not a system owned subverse that is.

When users enter a subverse we can either

  1. participate and abide by the rules/guidelines,

  2. participate but not follow the rules/guidelines and find our posts/comments removed,

  3. attempt to convince the moderator(s) to change the rules (while acknowledging that they are under no compulsion to accept suggestions), or

  4. leave the subverse

There is this ridiculous (IMO) idea floating around that Voats free speech ideal should mean that users can enter any subverse they want, post anything they want, and say anything they want in the comments, because, free speech!!! - and then feel all downtrodden and hard done by and yell censorship!!! if their post/comment is deleted - that's not he way it works.
